narr: A large ridge of high pressure was centered over the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley on July 25th, 2023. Convection developed along a lake breeze from Elyria, OH northeast to Erie, PA, just south of the I-90 corridor, as surface based CAPE values built to 2000-3000 j/kg by early afternoon. Little to no deep layer bulk shear promoted a pulse thunderstorm environment, with isolated thunderstorms building and collapsing within a 30-60 minute period. A few of the storms produced large hail and damaging winds from microbursts. One slow moving, back-building storm produced isolated flash flooding in the Chagrin Falls area.
ev: Intense, short duration rainfall event produced flash flooding in Chagrin Falls. Radar estimated 2 to 2.5 inches of rain fell in a 60 to 90 minute period, with a rain gauge measurement in Chagrin Falls of 2.1 inches of rain in less than one hour. Widespread street flooding was observed, including Solon Road and Monticello Drive near the Chagrin River, South Main Street and South Street in the southern portion of Chagrin Falls, and Bell Street near downtown Chagrin Falls. A few reports of flooded basements due to both flooded creeks and sewer backup.
